title: Coherence and finiteness of higher direct images
statement:
(Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1 (Tag
[02O5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O5)) and Lemma 30.19.2
(Tag [02O6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O6)).)
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism with $S$ locally Noetherian and let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is coherent for all
$i$; locally on $S$ (and globally if $S$ is quasi-compact)
$R^if_*\mathcal{F}=0$ for $i\gg0$; if $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with $A$ Noetherian
then the $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})$ are finite $A$-modules. (No bound uniform
over a non-quasi-compact $S$ exists in general: for
$S=\coprod_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Spec}k$, $X=\coprod_n\mathbf P^n_k$ and
$\mathcal F=\mathcal O(-n-1)$ on the $n$-th piece, $R^nf_*\mathcal F\ne0$
for every $n$.)

proof.text: Properness makes f quasi-compact and quasi-separated [pqf-lem-proper-basic], so [lem-pc-finite-support-hi] applies. Restricting to any affine open V of S gives vanishing in all sufficiently large degrees; these local statements glue, and a finite affine cover gives a global bound when S is quasi-compact.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1 (02O5) and Lemma 30.4.5 (01XJ)

proof.text: Coherence is local on S, so take S=Spec(A). The ring A is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]; f is of finite type [pqf-lem-proper-basic], so X is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply the devissage criterion [lem-pc-coherent-property-devissage] (Tag 01YI) to P(F) := "R^p f_*F is coherent for all p>=0". (0): R^pf_*0=0. (1): for 0->F_1->F_2->F_3->0 exact, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] (v=f_*, Mod(O_X) having enough injectives) gives the long exact sequence ... -> R^{p-1}f_*F_3 -> R^pf_*F_1 -> R^pf_*F_2 -> R^pf_*F_3 -> R^{p+1}f_*F_1 -> ...; if two of the F_i have P, each R^pf_* of the third sits in a five-term window whose four outer terms are coherent, so it is an extension of a kernel of a map of coherent modules by a cokernel of a map of coherent modules, hence coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum] (1),(2). Hypothesis (2) of the criterion is supplied in steps 3 and 4.

source.place: proof of Proposition 30.19.1 (02O5), first two paragraphs; Lemma 01YI (lemma-property)

proof.text: Let i:Z->X be an integral closed subscheme with generic point xi and g=f o i, proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] (b); Z is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] (g is separated of finite type by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]) there are a proper surjection pi:Z'->Z, a dense open U of Z with pi^{-1}(U)->U an isomorphism, and an immersion j:Z'->P^m_S over S. With g'=g o pi, proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], [lem-pc-chow-relative-ample] makes j a closed immersion, g' and pi projective, and L=j^*O(1) ample over affine opens of S and of Z. Z' is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so O_{Z'} is coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; [lem-pc-relative-kill-by-twisting] for g' over S and for pi over Z (F=O_{Z'}) gives n with R^p g'_*L^n=0 and R^q pi_*L^n=0 for p,q>0. Put G=pi_*L^n; it is coherent by [lem-pc-projective-coherent-higher-images] for the projective pi over the Noetherian Z (L^n is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]). Since Rpi_*L^n has cohomology only in degree 0 it is G[0], and [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] gives Rg'_*L^n = Rg_*G; hence R^pg_*G=R^pg'_*L^n=0 for p>0 and g_*G=g'_*L^n, which is coherent by [lem-pc-projective-coherent-higher-images] for g'.

source.place: proof of Proposition 30.19.1 (02O5), Chow and twisting paragraphs; Remark 30.18.2 (remark-chow-Noetherian)

proof.text: Put E=i_*G. It is coherent by [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology]. The closed immersion i is affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so R^qi_*G=0 for q>0 [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi], Ri_*G=E[0], and [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] gives Rf_*E=Rg_*G: R^pf_*E=R^pg_*G is 0 for p>0 and coherent for p=0 by step 3, so P(E) holds. Over U, G is isomorphic to the invertible module L^n on pi^{-1}(U)=U, so G_z is nonzero for z in U; Supp(G) is closed [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] and contains the dense U, so Supp(G)=Z and Supp(E)=i(Z). The generic point xi lies in U, so G_xi is free of rank one over O_{Z,xi}, which is the field kappa(xi) because Z is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]; E_xi=G_xi as an O_{X,xi}-module through the surjection O_{X,xi}->O_{Z,xi}=kappa(xi), so it is annihilated by m_xi and has dimension 1. This is hypothesis (2) of [lem-pc-coherent-property-devissage], which therefore gives P(F) for every coherent F, i.e. all R^pf_*F are coherent.

source.place: proof of Proposition 30.19.1 (02O5), paragraph on (Z -> X)_*G and the final sentences

proof.text: For S=Spec(A), properness supplies separatedness and quasi-compactness by [pqf-lem-proper-basic], and [lem-pc-cohomology-sections-affine-base] identifies H^i(X,F) with Gamma(S,R^i f_*F); its quasi-coherent hypothesis on F holds since F is coherent. By step 4 R^if_*F is coherent, hence quasi-coherent of finite type on the Noetherian S [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so its module of sections over the affine S is a finitely generated A-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. This proves the 02O6 finiteness clause.

blueprint_proof_text:
The vanishing for sufficiently large $i$, over each affine (or
quasi-compact) open of $S$, follows from the finite
affine-cover bound of [lem-pc-finite-support-hi].
If $f$ is projective, coherence and finite generation are
[lem-pc-projective-coherent-higher-images], applied locally on
the base.
For a general proper $f$ over a locally Noetherian base the assertion is
the recorded classical input named in the statement: Cohomology of
Schemes, Proposition 30.19.1 (Tag
[02O5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O5)) reads ``Let $S$
be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then
$R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is a coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module for all
$i\geq0$.'', and its proof reduces to the projective case by Chow's
lemma (Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.18.1, Tag
[0200](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0200)) together with the
twisting vanishing and the relative Leray spectral sequence; the affine
finiteness clause is Lemma 30.19.2 (Tag
[02O6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O6)). The statement of
this lemma, whose base is locally Noetherian, is exactly the proposition
cited, so it is discharged by the recorded input; the vanishing bound and
the projective case are in addition proved here, and every use below is
over a locally Noetherian base.
